title: F2 unblocked by Plan G close-out (commit 0715bc7)
body:
F2 sits in the Goal Governance V1 sequence at: F0 ✓ → F1 ✓ → G ✓ → F2 (this plan).

Prerequisites:
- F0 (2026-05-05-002): goal-gap config + GoalGapFinding/GoalGapClusterContext + classify_goal_gap_cluster (consumed via D007).
- F1 (2026-05-05-003): objective_contract schema + sufficiency auditor + plan-lock gate. F1 ships the resolution path (_resolve_goal_auditor_agent) F2/F002 wires into a real dispatcher.
- Plan G (2026-05-06-001): runtime evidence harness (web/iOS/Android/backend/common). G's captured EvidenceRef artifacts are exactly what F2/F001 walks against the contract's required_evidence list. G closed at commit 0715bc7 with all 6 features signed off (1251 tests passing); F2 unblock recorded in Plan G's D021.

Why: F1 deliberately left the post-impl half open because it needed runtime evidence to walk against. Now that G ships that surface, F2 closes the loop and provides the second half of goal-completion governance (F1 catches sufficiency gaps before lock; F2 catches completion gaps before close-out).

How to apply: F2 implementation MUST NOT modify F1 or Plan G surfaces. Any drift requires a new D-entry. The plan's `dependencies:` frontmatter cites all three prereq plans; subtree boundaries are enforced by the worktree-boundary verify step at every feature commit.

title: Single-repo plan in v1; substring matcher is a v1 coverage heuristic, not a semantic completion proof
body:
Existing agent-conventions v1.4.0 ObjectiveContract.completion_test.required_evidence (list of operator-supplied matcher strings) is sufficient for F2 v1. F2 keeps the matcher semantics as exact-substring against EvidenceRef.uri OR EvidenceRef.note — no regex, no structured rules, no journey-walk semantics.

**Critical framing — what the matcher IS and IS NOT:**

The substring matcher is a **v1 evidence-coverage heuristic**. It answers a single question per matcher string: 'is there at least one EvidenceRef whose uri or note contains this substring?' That's it.

The matcher CAN:
- flag missing evidence (no captured ref matches a required_evidence string → `missing_evidence` finding); this is the load-bearing signal F2 v1 ships.
- flag orphan journeys (a contract user_journey has zero captured refs at all → `journey_gap` finding).

The matcher CANNOT and MUST NOT claim:
- that a journey is functionally complete because some matcher hit;
- that captured artifacts actually demonstrate the behavior the contract describes;
- that artifact CONTENT is correct (the matcher only checks uri/note metadata, not bytes);
- that the absence of findings means the implementation is correct — only that no obvious evidence-coverage gaps were detected by this heuristic.

Negative direction (no match → missing) is sound: if the operator declared a required_evidence string and no captured ref carries it, that's a real gap. Positive direction (match → ?) is a heuristic only: a substring hit on uri/note tells you SOMETHING was captured under that label, not that the captured thing is the right thing.

Why:
1. The simplest matcher that could possibly work, per F2's goal of catching obvious completion gaps before close-out — not certifying journey correctness.
2. F1's pattern: ship the v1 with simple-as-possible primitives, let real use show what richer schema the next iteration needs. F1 took 4 review rounds (D076–D079) on the OSS-readiness slice to land its public boundary; we don't want to repeat that pressure on a schema bump that may or may not be needed.
3. Cross-repo boundary work (F1's F001 in agent-conventions + the F002 subtree-pull import) is a known cost. F1 absorbed it because the schema bump was load-bearing for the whole sequence. F2's increment doesn't have that pressure.
4. Honest framing prevents over-trust. Operators using `dontpanic plan close` should understand that a green completion audit means 'no obvious evidence gaps detected,' NOT 'the implementation is verified correct.' Behavioral completion proofs require richer schema (structured assertions, journey-walk steps) that v1 deliberately defers.

How to apply:
- F2 stays in DontPanic only. NO touches to claude/shared/, agent-conventions/, or v1.4.0 schemas. ALL F2 features ship in scripts/dontpanic_orchestrate/ and tests/ + this plan dir.
- F001's auditor docstring + completion_findings.json envelope MUST include a 'audit_kind: "v1_evidence_coverage_heuristic"' field at the top so downstream consumers (F003 plan-close gate, F2 dogfood disposition, future F2 follow-ups) read the correct semantics.
- F003 plan-close CLI on a passing audit MUST print 'no evidence-coverage gaps detected' (NOT 'plan complete') so the operator UX matches the heuristic's actual scope.
- Acceptance docstrings + tests must not assert 'completeness' anywhere; they assert 'gap detection.'
- D011 covers the abort condition if the substring matcher proves insufficient mid-impl. The richer schema (regex, structured assertions, behavioral journey-walks) is the v2 follow-up after real use shows the shape.

title: Cross-vendor dispatcher IS in scope — F002, the one place we don't defer
body:
F1's F005 dogfood ran with DONTPANIC_GOAL_AUDITOR_ALLOW_SAME_VENDOR=1 set (Claude served as both implementer AND auditor). That was acceptable for dogfood because it was operator-judged review, not adversarial. But F2 ships the production post-impl audit gate — close-out is exactly the boundary where adversarial review matters most.

Landing F2 without real cross-vendor dispatch would repeat the same-vendor caveat at the worst possible place: every plan's close-out gate would either silently same-vendor-pass or be permanently in offline-mode. Neither is acceptable.

F1 already shipped resolution: _resolve_goal_auditor_agent walks the precedence chain (per-call > project.roles.goal_auditor > global.roles.goal_auditor > legacy default_auditor > codex) and refuses same-vendor unless the override env is set. F2/F002 just wires the missing dispatch step: instantiate the resolved auditor from AGENT_REGISTRY, execute the prompt, parse the response.

Not in scope: iterative implementer↔auditor volley (single-pass dispatch in v1; iterative loop is queued for follow-up if real use shows it's needed). Not in scope: new auditor agents beyond claude/codex (existing F005a registry is sufficient).

Why this is the one non-deferred bit: every other 'defer to follow-up' answer to a lock-time question is reversible cheaply. Deferring cross-vendor dispatch isn't reversible cheaply because every plan that closes-out under the deferred regime carries the same-vendor caveat in its evidence trail. Better to pay the cost up front.

title: Override durability mirrors F1 F004 — input-bound SHA-256 hashes
body:
Operator override flag `--ignore-completion-findings <reason>` writes evidence/goal-governance/post_impl/override.json containing the reason + SHA-256 hashes of:
1. features.json (the canonical decomposition state)
2. resolved objective_contract file (the goal definition)
3. completion_findings.json (the F2 audit output that prompted the override)
4. evidence manifest (concatenated sorted-by-uri ref uris + hashes — captures any drift in the evidence tree)

On subsequent runs, F003 recomputes current input hashes; if any drift is detected, the override is treated as invalidated (same as if it didn't exist). Operator must re-issue the override flag for the new state.

Why:
- F004 of F1 used this exact pattern for sufficiency overrides (lock-time gate). Reusing the pattern keeps the operator mental model uniform across pre-impl and post-impl gates.
- Durable-but-input-bound is the right tradeoff: too durable (e.g. plain reason text only) and the override silently survives material changes; too ephemeral (e.g. override expires after N days) and operators have to repeatedly re-rationalize the same call without a clear trigger. Drift-invalidation ties refusal to a real signal.
- Evidence manifest hash is the new piece F2 adds (F1's F004 didn't have a manifest; F2 does because Plan G now produces EvidenceRef trees). Including it catches the case where the evidence is partially regenerated — operator must reconfirm the override applies to the new evidence shape.

How to apply: F003 implements `_compute_completion_input_hashes(plan_dir)` returning a dict of the four hashes; override.json stores reason + recorded_hashes; current run computes vs recorded; mismatch → discard override + treat run as un-overridden. Same as F004's `_compute_input_hashes` but with the additional manifest field.

title: Dogfood is plan-local static fixture in v1; not live historical plan
body:
F004 ships a synthetic completed-plan tree under evidence/dogfood/synthetic-plan/ with intentionally incomplete runtime evidence. Operator runs F001+F002+F003 against this tree and confirms the auditor surfaces materially-correct gaps in both classes (missing_evidence + journey_gap).

Real-plan dogfood (running F2 against e.g. F1's own evidence tree, or Plan G's close-out tree) is queued as a follow-up plan AFTER F004's synthetic-fixture path validates.

Why:
- F1's F005 dogfood used static curated fixtures (Spin & Dine + Glam) precisely because reproducibility matters. Operators need to be able to re-run the dogfood from a clean repo and get the same auditor output without external dependencies (running emulators, etc.). Plan G adapters are deferred-wired anyway in v1; live-plan dogfood would either need the deferred wiring to land first OR an offline-mode workaround.
- Static fixture dogfood proves the auditor logic is correct in isolation. Real-plan dogfood would also surface subtle interactions with project-specific evidence trees, but those interactions are out of v1's bounded scope. Better to land v1 with a tight reproducible bar, then expand.
- F1's pattern: F005 (dogfood) was the LAST feature in the F1 plan, gated on F001-F004 having shipped. F2 mirrors that ordering: F004 is the LAST feature here, gated on F001-F003 having shipped.

How to apply: F004 ships only fixtures + dispositions, no scripts/ diff. The fixture tree is committed and reproducible. Real-plan dogfood will be its own plan with its own decision log.

title: CLI yes (`dontpanic plan close <plan-id>`); MCP no in v1
body:
F003 ships the CLI surface; no MCP exposure of the plan-close gate in v1. External agent invocation can follow after the CLI behavior stabilizes.

Why:
- Plan G locked library-only at G's lock turn for the same reason: a stable CLI behavior is the prerequisite to a stable MCP wrap. Wrapping a still-evolving CLI in MCP creates two mutating surfaces simultaneously.
- The plan-close gate is the most consequential of the three CLI subcommands (lock / dispatch / close). It's the one where operator UX matters most: clear refusal messages, dry-run preview, exit-code matrix mapping to operator action. CLI-first lets us land that polish before exposing it to external agents.
- F003 mirrors F004 of F1 (`dontpanic plan lock`) which also shipped CLI-only. Once both CLI gates are stable, a follow-up plan can wrap both in MCP simultaneously with consistent semantics.

How to apply: F003 adds 'close' to the existing `dontpanic plan` subcommand router (next to 'lock'). NO mcp_server.py modifications in F2. NO new mcp tool exposure. Follow-up plan owns MCP surface decisions when CLI is stable.

title: F0 triage consumed unchanged via classify_goal_gap_cluster()
body:
F2 maps its CompletionFinding shape into F0's GoalGapFinding shape (severity / finding_id / issue / subsystem / journey) via a normalization helper; clusters by (subsystem, journey) with coherence_rule='subsystem_and_journey'; calls classify_goal_gap_cluster() per cluster to get the triage decision.

F2 does NOT redefine the taxonomy. F2 does NOT add new triage classes. F2 does NOT modify nested_orchestration's GoalGap{Finding,ClusterContext,Triage} types.

If during F001 implementation the F0 shape proves insufficient (e.g. F2 needs an additional severity tier, or the cluster context shape is wrong for completion-audit findings), F001 STOPS and surfaces a follow-up plan proposal to extend F0 — never inline-redefines.

Why:
- F0 (Plan 2026-05-05-002) is the canonical encoding of GOAL_GOVERNANCE_V1 §3.3 + §6.4 triage rules. F2 redefining or extending those rules in completion_auditor.py would split the truth surface and create silent drift between pre-impl (F1) and post-impl (F2) gating decisions.
- F1's pre-impl auditor consumes F0 the same way (sufficiency findings → GoalGapFinding shape → classify_goal_gap_cluster). Mirroring that pattern keeps the operator's mental model consistent: same triage applies whether the finding came from sufficiency or completion.
- The triage rules are intentionally simple (>=3 findings + medium-or-higher + subsystem_and_journey coherence → child_plan; small + low + fits-existing-feature → inline_fix; else operator_deferred). Extending them inline would invite ad-hoc rules that drift over time.

How to apply: F001 ships `to_goal_gap_findings()` adapter + `cluster_findings()` grouper + `make_cluster_context()` helper. F003 plan-close gate invokes classify_goal_gap_cluster() per cluster; the per-cluster triage class drives the block-or-pass decision.

title: No new runtime adapters in F2
body:
F2 does NOT ship new evidence-capture surfaces. The five sources covered by Plan G (web / iOS / Android / backend / harness composing all four) are sufficient for v1.

Future sources (e.g. desktop app screen capture, Slack-bot behavior capture, browser-extension surface, etc.) land in their own plans, not here. F2's scope is the audit layer: consume what's already captured, classify, gate close-out.

Why:
- Scope discipline. F2's locked answer to the operator's lock-time questions was 'no new runtime adapters'. Adding adapter work mid-plan would expand the implementation cost and confuse the dependency story (F2 must ship before its own adapters could complete a journey).
- Plan G's adapters are deferred-wired in v1 anyway (Playwright session, simctl session, adb session, firebase_admin session — all stub-seam-only with deferred production wiring). Adding more deferred adapters would just add more deferred work without unblocking F2.
- Operators who need a new evidence source for their plan's close-out audit can write a custom EvidenceSource (per Plan G F005's swap seam) — no F2 plan modification needed.

How to apply: F2 implementation diff stays out of scripts/dontpanic_orchestrate/runtime_evidence/. Greppable boundary check at every F-commit confirms zero diffs to G's adapter modules.

title: Capture-only invariant carried forward — F2 reads, never captures
body:
Plan G D002 locked the harness as capture-only. F2 carries this forward at the audit layer: F2 reads existing EvidenceRef artifacts (rebuilt from the on-disk evidence tree), it does NOT invoke G's adapters during the audit run.

F001's `_build_evidence_manifest()` walks `evidence/goal-governance/post_impl/<source>/<journey>/<filename>` and rehashes artifact bytes to reconstruct EvidenceRef instances. It never instantiates a WebDriver / IosDriver / AndroidDriver / BackendProvider. The manifest rebuild is purely filesystem-IO + sha256 hashing.

Why:
- Audit-time invocation of capture adapters would be both expensive (booting simulators / emulators / Firebase project access during close-out) and wrong (capture should happen at feature close-out time, when the dev's local environment is set up; not at plan close-out time, which may be a different operator session).
- Plan G's invariant is operationally important for F2's correctness: if F2 could re-capture, it could mask gaps by re-running flaky test paths. Read-only audit forces operators to commit the capture artifacts they want audited.
- v2 follow-up: G could emit a manifest file directly at adapter-write time, removing the need for F2 to self-rebuild. v1 self-rebuilds because adding a manifest emit to G post-close would be modifying G after it shipped (no D-entry for that).

How to apply: F001 module-level docstring asserts the invariant. Tests confirm `_build_evidence_manifest` doesn't import any runtime_evidence/ session classes (greppable assertion). F003 plan-close gate refuses to dispatch if no evidence tree exists at the expected path — does NOT auto-capture the missing evidence.

title: Dispatch-time backstop on plan-close path — mirror of F004 plan-lock backstop
body:
Hand-edited active→completed flips (operator opens plan.md and changes status manually, bypassing `dontpanic plan close`) are caught at the next supervisor entrypoint that consults plan status. The backstop verifies that any plan with status='completed' has either:
- evidence/goal-governance/post_impl/completion_findings.json (the F2 audit output), OR
- evidence/goal-governance/post_impl/override.json (the operator-honored override).

Missing both → BackstopError: completed status without F2 audit evidence at <plan-id>. Supervisor halts before dispatch.

Why:
- F004 of F1 added the same backstop pattern at the plan-lock boundary (caught hand-edited draft→active flips that lacked sufficiency evidence). F2 mirrors this for the plan-close boundary.
- The motivation is identical: a CLI gate that operators can bypass by hand-editing plan.md isn't a real gate — it's a recommendation. The backstop turns it into an actual gate by failing fast at any subsequent dispatch.
- The backstop is read-only: it doesn't mutate the plan back to 'active' or auto-revert the flip. It surfaces the missing evidence to the operator, who then either runs `dontpanic plan close` properly or commits a deliberate override.
- Catching at next-tool-action vs immediate is the right tradeoff: immediate would require filesystem watching (over-engineered); never-catching is the bypass surface F004 already proved unacceptable.

How to apply: F003 adds a single check function (e.g. `enforce_completion_gate(plan_dir)`) called from supervisor.py's plan-load path, alongside F004's `enforce_sufficiency_gate`. Idempotent + read-only + raises BackstopError on violation. Tests confirm hand-edit detection.

title: Schema-insufficiency abort condition (D002 release valve)
body:
If during F001 implementation the substring-matcher approach proves insufficient (e.g. operators routinely need regex / structured matchers / journey-walk semantics to express their intent), F001 STOPS and surfaces a cross-repo schema-bump proposal BEFORE committing F001.

The abort signal is concrete: the impl turn cannot satisfy F001's acceptance items (esp. acceptance #1 — `run_completion_audit` returning a list[CompletionFinding]) without one of:
- richer matcher shape (regex, structured-field assertions),
- additional ObjectiveContract fields (per-rule severity, per-rule journey binding),
- new EvidenceRef metadata not present in v1.4.0.

If any of those is needed, F2 splits like F1 did: an agent-conventions feature out front (F000 in agent-conventions) + a subtree-pull import feature in DontPanic + the existing F001-F004 features. The abort recognizes the cross-repo cost is appropriate when the simple shape genuinely doesn't fit.

Why:
- D002 locked single-repo + simple matcher as the v1 default. D011 is the release valve that prevents implementer-pressure-to-ship from forcing an inadequate shape into the codebase.
- F1's pattern: F1 didn't have an abort condition because the schema bump (objective_contract.schema.json + completion_test) was load-bearing from the start. F2 has the option to stay single-repo because the schema is already there; the abort exists for the case where it turns out the existing schema is the wrong shape after all.
- Better to surface the cost up-front than ship a v1 that operators have to work around with naming conventions in their matcher strings (a known anti-pattern).

How to apply: F001 implementer monitoring this signal during step list. Concrete trigger: if step 7 (the `_match_required_evidence` impl) cannot be written as substring-against-uri-OR-note while still passing all F001 acceptance items, STOP and write a cross-repo split proposal as a separate decision/D-entry; commit nothing of F001 until the operator approves the split. Default expectation: substring is sufficient and the abort never fires.

title: F001 ship — completion auditor module + 26 tests; ObjectiveContract schema-path correction
body:
F001 implemented and verified. Ship surface: scripts/dontpanic_orchestrate/completion_auditor.py (606 lines) + scripts/dontpanic_orchestrate/tests/test_completion_auditor.py (536 lines, 26 tests).

What shipped:
- Public surface: run_completion_audit(plan_dir) -> list[CompletionFinding]; CompletionFinding (Pydantic, extra='forbid', severity validated against F0 _GOAL_GAP_SEVERITY_RANK); CompletionFindingsEnvelope with audit_kind: Literal['v1_evidence_coverage_heuristic'] (D002 load-bearing); COMPLETION_GAP_CLASSES=('missing_evidence','journey_gap','integration_gap'); COMPLETION_AUDIT_KIND constant; COMPLETION_FINDINGS_ARTIFACT='completion_findings.json'; CompletionAuditError; F0 adapters to_goal_gap_findings / cluster_findings / make_cluster_context.
- Internal helpers: _load_objective_contract (frontmatter + JSON, mirror of F1's pattern); _build_evidence_manifest (filesystem IO + sha256 hash; rebuilds EvidenceRef list from evidence/goal-governance/post_impl/<source>/<journey>/<filename>; D009 capture-only — no runtime_evidence imports); _match_required_evidence (substring against uri OR note; empty matcher → no match); _emit_journey_gaps (severity='high' per orphan journey); _emit_missing_evidence (severity='medium' default).
- Module + run_completion_audit docstrings carry D002 framing greppably: 'v1 evidence-coverage heuristic' + 'NOT a semantic completion proof' (whitespace-tolerant regex tests enforce both).
- Greppable invariant test (no runtime_evidence session-class imports) confirms D009 capture-only carry-forward.

ObjectiveContract schema-path correction: Plan F2 description (locked) refers to 'the contract's completion_test.required_evidence' string list. The actual v1.4.0 schema (claude/shared/schemas/v1.0/models/objective_contract_model.py) places required_evidence at ObjectiveContract TOP LEVEL: `required_evidence: list[str] | None`; completion_test is a separate prose-string field. F001 implements against the correct shape (top-level list[str]). The substring-matcher contract is unchanged — D011 abort condition does NOT fire because the matcher remains list[str] regardless of nesting. Plan description not amended (locked); future readers should treat F2's plan.md and feature description references to 'completion_test.required_evidence' as a pre-impl drafting error and read 'ObjectiveContract.required_evidence' instead.

Verification:
- F001 tests: 26/26 pass.
- Full orchestrate suite: 1277 passed, 7 skipped, 0 regressions.
- ruff check: clean.
- ruff format --check: clean.
- python3 scripts/sanitization_check.py: clean (823 files scanned).
- Worktree boundary: zero diffs to claude/shared/, F1 surfaces (sufficiency_auditor.py + sufficiency_gate.py), or Plan G runtime_evidence/ adapters. F001 ships only completion_auditor.py + its test file + this D-entry.

Why: F001 is the plan-text-only orchestration core that F002 (cross-vendor dispatcher) and F003 (plan-close gate + CLI) consume. Pinning audit_kind as a Literal ensures F003 cannot mistakenly read v1 findings as a semantic completion proof. The substring matcher is deliberately operator-supplied + metadata-only; the auditor flags coverage gaps (no captured ref matches a declared required_evidence string) but does NOT certify journey correctness — that bar requires a richer schema and is queued for v2.

How to apply: F002 and F003 import from completion_auditor by name. F002 calls run_completion_audit on the plan's contract, then passes the resulting envelope to the cross-vendor goal-auditor (Codex when implementer was Claude) for adversarial review. F003's plan-close gate consumes the audit transcript + envelope; refusal-on-blocking-findings logic gates active→completed. Future readers: D002's IS/IS-NOT framing is the load-bearing semantic boundary; preserve it in v2 follow-ups.
